reviewed_by: Codex scoped process-worker experiment review; independent causal validation by validate_cpu_scaling
reason: One Core coordinator delegates pure PDF layout to an explicitly injected bounded process pool. The selected cases cover exact process/loop/request-context ownership, FIFO and count/byte admission, queued/running cancellation, startup/exit/replacement/shutdown, PDF equivalence/artifact integrity/cache/revision/auth and preserved harness ledgers. Butler adds fresh authenticated project/global/managed host-load reads, unknown values, shared off-loop sampling, discovery/help/catalog, packaged source digest and Chroma synchronization including actual Core startup. One frontend metadata case covers current host-load discovery terms. The committed owned-LAN driver and raw matrix/overload/fault/soak evidence exercise these boundaries separately; no full suite is selected.
exclusions: No full suites. The CPU prototype is constructor-injected and leaves the shipped default unchanged. Butler adds read-only live host-capacity discovery and one focused frontend catalog metadata case; no new controls, geometry, browser-origin or authentication behavior. Native/Playwright suites are outside these boundaries. No production data, live providers or security tools. Local Python3.12; focused CI coverage selects3.11/3.12/3.13 for spawned-process lifecycle. Frozen/native packaging, Windows/macOS execution and whole-Core horizontal scaling remain outside the prototype.
